name: Congressman Jim Clyburn — The First Eight: A Personal History of the Pioneering Black Congressmen Who Shaped a Nation
location: Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute at Hunter College

short_name: A Personal History of the Pioneering Black Congressmen Who Shaped a Nation

name: Special Waste Drop-Off
description: Safely dispose of harmful household products like motor oil, batteries, and fluorescent bulbs that are illegal to throw in trash or recycling. This service is free for all NYC residents at various sites in all five boroughs.

name: Line Dance Fitness
description: Line up and get ready to move in this high-energy line dance fitness class. It is a fun way to improve cardiovascular health and coordination through synchronized movement.

name: Zumba Gold®
description: A low-impact workout set to a fusion of Latin, International, and popular music dance themes. This dynamic fitness system is designed to be effective and exciting for all levels.

name: Forest Fridays @ Van Cortlandt Park
description: Join volunteers to save the forest floor by removing invasive species like Bush Honeysuckle and Multiflora Rose. This winter initiative is critical for protecting native plants while they are dormant.

name: Volunteering at Conference House Park - The Blue Wave
description: Participate in a self-directed beach and park clean-up initiative. Volunteers help remove debris and maintain the beauty of the Staten Island waterfront.

name: Afro-Latin Jazz Orchestra with a Tribute to Chilo Cajigas
description: El Museo del Barrio and Belongó launch a new multi-engagement residency featuring a performance by the Afro-Latin Jazz Orchestra. The residency deepens the presence of Belongó in East Harlem through a significant cultural collaboration.

name: Gibney Company APAP Showing for Performing Arts Presenters
description: An annual showing for performing arts presenters featuring Gibney Company performing excerpts from Johan Inger works in their current repertory. The program includes pieces such as Rain Dogs, When It Was, and Bliss.
short_name: Gibney Company APAP Showing for Performing Arts Presenters

name: Titanique
description: A comedic musical parody that sets the story of the Titanic to the powerhouse hits of Celine Dion. This high-energy show offers a campy and hilarious retelling of the classic love story.

name: The Play That Goes Wrong
description: An Olivier Award-winning comedy where an amateur drama troupe attempts to stage a murder mystery that quickly falls apart. It is a masterclass in slapstick humor, stage mishaps, and theatrical disaster.

name: Gazillion Bubble Show
description: An interactive spectacle featuring incredible bubble artistry, laser lighting effects, and magical bubble stunts. This long-running family-friendly show invites the audience into a world of visual wonder.

name: Winter Jazz Fest - The Loft
description: Experience the vibrant sounds of the Winter Jazz Fest in the intimate setting of The Loft at City Winery. This festival showcase features innovative jazz artists performing in one of NYC's premier listening rooms.

name: Winter Jazz Fest - Main Stage
description: The Winter Jazz Fest continues with a special Main Stage performance held in the expansive atmosphere of The Loft. Enjoy a curated lineup of world-class jazz musicians as part of this annual city-wide celebration.

name: Friday @ Out Of Ordinary • Open Bar! 2 for 1 Drinks! Everyone FREE w/ RSVP
description: Kick off the weekend at this Brooklyn venue featuring an open bar, 2-for-1 drink specials, and free entry for those who RSVP. It is a high-energy social event designed for nightlife enthusiasts.

name: The Amphitheaters
description: A live music performance by The Amphitheaters on the Young Ethels stage.

name: Live Bands: Good Time Mystery Vision // Boulevard Bushmen // Digamy
description: An evening of live music featuring performances by Good Time Mystery Vision, Boulevard Bushmen, and Digamy.
short_name: Good Time Mystery Vision // Boulevard Bushmen // Digamy

name: Ceramics Studio Time - 4-session access block
description: Flexible open studio access block for ceramic artists to work on independent projects with access to pottery wheels and hand-building tables. Clay must be purchased through the makerspace and glaze firing fees apply based on size.

name: Shelter from the Storm: An Artist’s Eye with Stan Allen and Polly Apfelbaum
description: Shelter from the Storm features a collaborative effort between Stan Allen and Polly Apfelbaum, blending architecture and contemporary art. The show examines thematic links between environment, protection, and spatial aesthetics.

name: Revisiting the World of Tomorrow: The 1964-65 World's Fair
location: NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS)
description: An onsite exhibit exploring the 1964-1965 World’s Fair through images, brochures, and ephemera from the Municipal Archives. The display focuses on key areas of the fair including transportation, religion, and commerce.

name: Windows on the Archives
location: NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS)
description: A permanent onsite exhibit displaying the breadth of the City's documentary treasures from the Municipal Archives. The exhibit features records spanning over 300 years of governing and protecting the people of New York City.

name: WSCAH’s 86th Street Market
location: St. Paul & St. Andrew United Methodist Church
description: Each month, customers can receive a regular distribution of USDA MyPlate Balanced groceries. These packages contain a variety of healthy items, including grains, proteins, dairy products, and fresh fruits and vegetables.

name: Faith & Fun Friday: Kids Edition
location: St. Paul & St. Andrew United Methodist Church
description: Kids ages 4 through 10 are invited to join the church for crafts, games, dinner and fun. Parents are welcome to stay or drop off their kids for two hours of kid-free time.

name: Youth Group New Years Party
location: St. Paul & St. Andrew United Methodist Church
description: Middle and high school youth are invited to kick off 2026 with a party featuring dinner and King Cake making. The evening will include dreaming and visioning for the year ahead with Pastor Sally.

name: Heathers Screening & Talkback
location: St. Paul & St. Andrew United Methodist Church
description: A special screening of the cult classic film Heathers presented by the CWP Film Center. The event includes an in-person talkback with actor Christian Slater.

name: Primeval Ground [deep, unfathomable]
description: A group exhibition featuring ten artists exploring monochrome and low-chrome artworks across media like photography, weaving, and sculpture. The exhibit includes a panel discussion on Jan 15 and a movement drawing workshop on Jan 24.

name: Video of “Stories Around the Table”
description: A filmed performance featuring current and past members of a writing group that has met for 40 years to discuss aging and creativity. The collective share personal stories sitting around the table, reflecting a rich history of theatrical and literary collaboration.

name: Calling Choreographers: WestFest Dance 2026 Open Call
description: An invitation for choreographers to submit applications for the WestFest Dance 2026 festival. This online application period is open to performing artists seeking to showcase their work in the upcoming season.

name: Somewhere Funny, Nowhere Serious!
description: Somewhere Nowhere NYC transforms into an intimate speakeasy-style comedy club featuring a live stand-up showcase with big-name comedians as seen on Netflix and HBO.

name: Winter Realm Cinema
description: Winter Realm Cinema is a seasonal rooftop film experience in Midtown featuring a fully enclosed and heated terrace with stunning Manhattan views. The program offers a curated selection of cult films, classics, and new releases enjoyed via state-of-the-art wireless headphones. Guests can also enjoy a full bar and classic cinema concessions like fresh popcorn and hot dogs through March 1st.

name: Eternal Nature: Immersive Digital Art Exhibition
description: Experience 'Eternal Nature,' a multisensory digital art exhibition featuring immersive landscapes like crashing waterfalls and blooming forests. The gallery also showcases a landmark collaboration with the Musée d'Orsay, reimagining masterpieces by Monet and Van Gogh through light, sound, and scent.

name: Penguin Feeding
description: Join zoo staff to learn about the diet and habits of the zoo's resident penguins during their scheduled afternoon meal.

name: Junior Tennis Development Program
description: A comprehensive after-school tennis program for students aged 7 to 17, focusing on technical drills, strategic points, and match play. Participants are placed based on age and ability to ensure individual attention and development of sportsmanship.

name: Weekend DJ Sets
description: Every Friday and Saturday night, local DJs take over the decks to play a curated selection of vinyl and digital tracks. Expect a soul-heavy mix to keep the dance floor moving late into the night.

name: Wunderkammer III
description: Wunderkammer III is an ongoing exhibition located in the Lobby Gallery of Klapper Hall. This exhibition presents a 'cabinet of curiosities' featuring various items from the museum's permanent collection. It is currently open to visitors while the main museum undergoes installation.

name: Karaoke Friday
description: Join the Gottscheer Hall community for their signature Friday night karaoke. Experience a wide selection of German beers and pub eats while enjoying or participating in an evening of singing and entertainment.

name: Live Music
description: Grand Vin hosts live music performances Wednesday through Saturday nights, creating a sophisticated ambiance for dining and drinks. Guests can enjoy a rotating selection of musicians while exploring the venue's curated wine list and Italian-inspired menu.

name: Free First Fridays: Silkscreen T-Shirt Printing
description: Create your own personalized silkscreened t-shirt with designs inspired by film, music, and activism during this free community event. This session is supported by the Art Bridges Foundation’s Access for All program.

name: New York Latin American Art Triennial
description: This exhibition showcases contemporary works from Latin American artists as part of the city-wide Triennial event. The gallery presents a diverse range of artistic practices and cultural perspectives through mixed media installations.
short_name: New York Latin American Art Triennial

name: Nutcracker Rouge
description: A perennial smash hit burlesque reimagining of the classic holiday tale featuring a hedonistic mix of circus, opera, and cabaret. This Drama Desk-nominated production is a sensual blend of music hall and theater in an opulent Brooklyn palace.

name: Cocktail Magique
description: A spectacular farewell run of this playful burlesque revue that blends world-class magic with tantalizing variety acts and bespoke cocktails. After over 575 performances, this immersive production takes its final bow on February 8.

name: A Taste of Thailand: Pad See Ew & Papaya Salad
description: Learn the cultural history of Thai cuisine and traditional techniques to create flavor-packed classics like Pad See Ew and Papaya Salad. Learn to season and cook flat rice noodles without compromising on authentic street food flavors.

name: Inuuteq Storch: Soon Will Summer Be Over
description: This exhibition features the photography of Inuuteq Storch, documenting the sublime landscapes and intimate daily life of Greenland. Through a personal lens, the artist explores themes of identity, environment, and cultural heritage.
short_name: Inuuteq Storch: Soon Will Summer Be Over

name: Vaginal Davis: Magnificent Product
description: A major exhibition spanning five decades of Vaginal Davis’s practice as a performer, visual artist, author, and countercultural icon. The presentation highlights her role as an underground trailblazer in queer politics and her uncompromising glamour.

name: Four Dilations
description: Four Dilations presents artistic positions that challenge dominant contemporary methods of timekeeping. The title references the physical phenomenon of temporal dilation, where time passes at different rates for observers in different frames of reference.

name: Gabrielle Goliath: Personal Accounts
description: This video series responds to the impacts of patriarchal violence across global contexts from Johannesburg to Kyiv. The installation intimately documents survivor testimonials by focusing on the sighs, breaths, and moments between spoken words.

name: Homeroom: LA ESCUELA___ Education as Resistance
description: Artist-run platform LA ESCUELA___ initiates a collective learning project charting radical pedagogies from across Latin America. This program explores how education can serve as a form of resistance within contemporary art spaces.

name: Ayoung Kim: Delivery Dancer Codex
description: Artist Ayoung Kim presents the US debut of her Delivery Dancer trilogy, utilizing generative AI and videogame engines to create narratives. Her work explores the collision of geopolitics, digital technologies, and synthesized mythologies.

name: The Housemaid

name: Rewind by Whisbe
description: A contemporary art installation by artist WhIsBe featuring oversized childhood toy sculptures ranging from 6 to 16 feet tall. The display includes pieces like a 10-foot rocket ship and a 15-foot dinosaur, reflecting on innocence and resilience.

name: Friday Feel-Good Improv Jam
description: Kick off the weekend with a high-energy, supportive improv jam open to all. Whether you're a seasoned pro or a first-timer, this jam is all about having fun and making good choices on stage.

name: Character Counts Open Mic

name: UNIQLO Friday Nights

name: ITMATTERS ft: Santi Espinosa, Audrey Mora, Brian Grossi, Joe Russell

name: Francesco De Carlo, Jon Fisch, Ayanna Dookie, Christine Berg

short_name: Francesco De Carlo, Jon Fisch, Ayanna Dookie, Christine Berg

name: Chuck Nice, Marina Franklin, Dante Nero, Jason Choi

name: Marion Grodin, Francesco De Carlo, Ayanna Dookie, Josh Adam Meyers

short_name: Marion Grodin, Francesco De Carlo, Ayanna Dookie, Josh Adam Meyers

name: Marina Franklin, Dante Nero, Christine Berg, Sean Donnelly

short_name: Marina Franklin, Dante Nero, Christine Berg, Sean Donnelly

name: Brendan Sagalow, Ashley Austin Morris, Jason Choi, Alexis Bradby, Nick Viagas

name: Smalls Afternoon Jam Session Hosted by Andrew Kushnir

short_name: Smalls Afternoon Jam Session Hosted by Andrew Kushnir

name: Vanessa Rubin and Her Trio

name: Rachel Z Quartet

name: Eric Wyatt Quartet

name: Against Time: The Noguchi Museum 40th Anniversary Reinstallation
description: This special reinstallation celebrates the 40th anniversary of The Noguchi Museum by showcasing the enduring vision of Isamu Noguchi. The exhibition highlights the history of the museum and its unique integration of building and garden.

name: Adult Cooking Class — Tasty Thai

name: Melissa Aldana Quartet

name: Bird and Nature Walk: Mount Loretto Unique Area

name: Milo Rau & Édouard Louis: The Interrogation

name: The Westerlies Play Bill Frisell: Album Release Show
description: This brass quartet premieres never-before-heard compositions from Bill Frisell's recent notebooks and highlights from his catalog.

name: Tony Trischka In Residence: Great Big World
description: Banjoist Tony Trischka performs a wide-ranging program exploring diverse musical landscapes and global influences.

name: Mike Gordon

name: Rain Garden Stewardship Volunteer Days
description: Help manage vital urban water systems by maintaining the rain gardens at Queens Botanical Garden. Stewardship activities include weeding, pruning, and learning about native plant species.

name: oskar med k: Make Me Feel Tour 2026

description: Nikolaj Szeps-Znaider leads Bruch’s Violin Concerto No. 1 and Elgar’s legendary Enigma Variations.

name: Ernest: Live from the South Tour

name: Teacher, Teacher: Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s Serpent’s Path and Chime

name: morning dew: cyanotype & natural toners

short_name: The Albertine Book Club Reads "Free Day" by Inès Cagnati

name: Golda Schultz Sings Barber & Stravinsky
location: David Geffen Hall at Lincoln Center
description: Soprano Golda Schultz joins conductor Kwamé Ryan for Samuel Barber’s Knoxville: Summer of 1915. The program also features the world premiere of a new work by George Lewis.

name: Bell X1 & Dowry Strings

name: kwn

description: An intimate evening featuring Jonathan Cohen and Gy Mirano as they discuss their latest artistic project. The event explores the intersection of performance and literature.
